item.text:
**Assessment:** probably no. I found limited procedural positives, but the 2024 record is dominated by repression, arrests, and a closed civic-space environment rather than genuine acceptance that power is contestable through free, fair, and meaningful elections.

- **[Freedom in the World 2025 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2025)** | Freedom House | 2025 | Claim: the report says Abiy-era electoral-law and NEBE reforms improved electoral operations and encouraged more opposition participation, and that some outstanding legislative/regional elections held in June 2024 were peaceful and credible according to AU observers. | IDs: 4B.1
- **[World Report 2024: Ethiopia](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-12 | Claim: opposition parties still faced restrictions on assembly, harassment, arrest, and detention in defiance of court orders, which points to a political arena that was not meaningfully contestable. | IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.9
- **[Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-04 | Claim: HRW reported the detention of an opposition spokesperson and a journalist, and concluded that no one appeared safe from arbitrary arrest; this is direct evidence against free political contestation. | IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.9
- **[Ethiopia: Journalist arrested under state of emergency: Belay Manaye](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr25/7782/2024/en/)** | Amnesty International | 2024-03-14 | Claim: Amnesty said a journalist was held under emergency powers for reporting on the Amhara conflict, and that other journalists had also been arbitrarily arrested under the state of emergency. | IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.9
- **[Ethiopia - Civicus Monitor](https://monitor.civicus.org/press_release/2024/ethiopia/)** | CIVICUS Monitor | 2024-12-04 | Claim: civic space was downgraded to “Closed” amid conflict and emergency measures, with surveillance, harassment, intimidation, and threats used against journalists and opposition members. | IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.9
- **[Ethiopia authorities suspend three rights groups](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | Claim: the government suspended three rights groups while Abiy praised reforms, which looks like selective punishment of civic actors rather than acceptance of robust electoral competition. | IDs: 4B.1, 3B.8

Search gap: I did not find a 2024 primary-source statement from Abiy clearly accepting the possibility of losing power in a free election. The strongest positive material is procedural and observer-based, not a direct democratic commitment.
